questions.prompt: What do a Malleable C2 profile's application-layer disguises (jQuery, OneDrive, Amazon) fail to change?
options: Nothing — a well-configured profile defeats all detection
The underlying TLS handshake characteristics that JA3/JA3S/JA4 fingerprint, which are largely independent of the application-layer disguise
questions.explanation: Malleable profiles disguise the application layer, but the TLS Client/Server Hello characteristics JA3/JA3S/JA4 capture are largely separate from that disguise.

questions.prompt: Why was JA4 developed as a successor to JA3?
options: JA3 was discontinued by its creators
JA4 was designed specifically to raise the cost of JA3-randomization tools attackers use to evade JA3 alone
JA4 only works on DNS traffic, not TLS
JA3 never worked correctly for Cobalt Strike specifically
questions.explanation: As JA3-randomizing evasion tools became common, JA4 was built to be more robust against exactly that evasion technique.

questions.prompt: What behavioral signature survives regardless of which Malleable C2 profile is applied?
options: Beacon rhythm at regular intervals with low jitter variance, and short sessions with low data volume per check-in
The file extension of the payload
questions.explanation: Regardless of application-layer disguise, the underlying periodic check-in pattern with consistent, low data volume remains a behavioral tell — the same statistical periodicity NetFlow analysis teaches you to spot.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson explicitly warn against relying on JA3/JA4 alone?
options: JA3/JA4 fingerprinting doesn't actually work in practice
A sophisticated operator can deliberately randomize their TLS fingerprint — fingerprinting should be one signal among several, not a single silver bullet
JA3/JA4 only detects Cobalt Strike, no other frameworks
TLS fingerprinting requires decrypting the traffic first
questions.explanation: Advanced operators can use JA3-randomizing tooling — fingerprinting is strongest combined with named-pipe indicators, beacon rhythm, and process-injection artifacts together, not relied on in isolation.
